stem_text: The velocity at which 6 kg mass (shown in figure) strikes the ground when it is released from a height of 6 m above the ground is ____ m/s . Assume pulley is massless and string is light and inextensible. (Take g=10m/s^(2) ) [FIG-stem-1]

candidate_solve.assumed_parameters_from_coaching_figure: Opposing suspended mass m = 2 kg, released from rest at height h = 6 m for M = 6 kg.
candidate_solve.derivation: Conservation of mechanical energy for connected two-body system: Delta K = W_net => 1/2(M+m)v^2 = (M-m)gh => v = sqrt(2(M-m)gh / (M+m)) = sqrt(2(6-2)(10)(6)/(6+2)) = sqrt(480/8) = sqrt(60) approx 7.74596 m/s.
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If m = M, v = 0 (equilibrium). If m = 0, v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(120) approx 10.95 m/s. Bound: 0 < 7.746 < 10.95 m/s.

sl2.crux: Setting up the coupled two-body kinetic energy ledger where both bodies move at identical instantaneous speed v while one descends and the other ascends.

representation_translation.evidence: Interpreting pulley system schematic to assign mass parameters.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Combined kinetic energy and potential energy ledger to speed.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Must avoid treating 6 kg mass as unconstrained free fall.

wrong_route_hypotheses.route: Single body free fall v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(120) = 10.95 m/s
Omitting m in kinetic energy denominator v = sqrt(2(M-m)gh / M) = 8.94 m/s
